note: Public-domain portraits from Wikimedia Commons, resized; see each source page.

portraits.name: John Snow
portraits.blurb: Physician who mapped London's 1854 cholera deaths to the Broad Street pump, a founding moment for epidemiology.

portraits.name: Isaac Newton
portraits.blurb: Mathematician and physicist; laws of motion, universal gravitation and calculus.

portraits.name: Pierre Charles Alexandre Louis
portraits.blurb: Physician whose 'numerical method' counted outcomes and showed bloodletting did little for pneumonia.

portraits.name: Ignaz Semmelweis
portraits.blurb: Obstetrician who showed that handwashing with chlorinated lime prevented childbed fever.

portraits.name: Baruch Spinoza
portraits.blurb: Philosopher of a single substance, Deus sive Natura; a lens grinder by trade.

portraits.name: Florence Nightingale
portraits.blurb: Nurse and statistician whose polar-area diagrams showed most Crimean War deaths were preventable.

portraits.name: James Lind
portraits.blurb: Naval surgeon who ran one of the first controlled trials, citrus against scurvy in 1747.

portraits.name: Ada Lovelace
portraits.blurb: Mathematician who wrote the first published algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine.

portraits.name: William Farr
portraits.blurb: Statistician who built England's system of vital statistics and cause-of-death classification.

portraits.name: Edward Jenner
portraits.blurb: Country doctor who showed cowpox inoculation protects against smallpox.

portraits.name: René Descartes
portraits.blurb: Philosopher and mathematician; methodic doubt and the coordinate plane.

portraits.name: Girolamo Fracastoro
portraits.blurb: Physician who proposed that 'seeds' of contagion spread disease, and named syphilis.

portraits.name: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
portraits.blurb: Draper of Delft whose hand-ground lenses first revealed bacteria and protozoa.

portraits.name: Mary Somerville
portraits.blurb: Mathematician and science writer whose work hinted at a planet beyond Uranus.

portraits.name: Louis Pasteur
portraits.blurb: Chemist behind germ theory, pasteurisation and vaccines for anthrax and rabies.

portraits.name: Elizabeth Blackwell
portraits.blurb: First woman to receive a medical degree in the United States (1849).

portraits.name: Michel de Montaigne
portraits.blurb: Inventor of the essay; 'Que sais-je?' What do I know?

portraits.name: Robert Koch
portraits.blurb: Microbiologist who identified the causes of tuberculosis and cholera; Koch's postulates.

portraits.name: Rudolf Virchow
portraits.blurb: Pathologist of 'omnis cellula e cellula' and an early voice for social medicine.

portraits.name: Charles Darwin
portraits.blurb: Naturalist of evolution by natural selection.

portraits.name: Mary Seacole
portraits.blurb: Jamaican-Scottish nurse who ran the British Hotel for soldiers in the Crimean War.

portraits.name: René Laennec
portraits.blurb: Physician who invented the stethoscope and described its sounds.

portraits.name: Émilie du Châtelet
portraits.blurb: Natural philosopher whose translation of Newton's Principia is still the standard French one.

portraits.name: Andreas Vesalius (attributed portrait)
portraits.blurb: Anatomist of De humani corporis fabrica, built on his own dissections.

portraits.name: Santiago Ramón y Cajal
portraits.blurb: Neuroscientist who showed the nervous system is made of separate neurons.

portraits.name: Gregor Mendel
portraits.blurb: Friar whose pea experiments uncovered the laws of inheritance.

portraits.name: William Harvey
portraits.blurb: Physician who demonstrated the circulation of the blood.

portraits.name: Mary Wollstonecraft
portraits.blurb: Philosopher, author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman.

portraits.name: Joseph Lister
portraits.blurb: Surgeon who introduced antiseptic surgery with carbolic acid.

portraits.name: Alexander von Humboldt
portraits.blurb: Naturalist and explorer who saw nature as one interconnected web.

portraits.name: Hippocrates
portraits.blurb: Physician of Kos, father of medicine; disease has natural causes.

portraits.name: Sofya Kovalevskaya
portraits.blurb: Mathematician of partial differential equations; first woman full professor in northern Europe.

portraits.name: Pierre-Simon Laplace
portraits.blurb: Mathematician of celestial mechanics and probability, the 'rule of succession'.

portraits.name: Aristotle
portraits.blurb: Philosopher who classified animals by dissection and founded formal logic.
